answer: Resist Sybil attacks by weighting influence with locked stake, not headcount. A common kernel registry binds each agent to a published bond; splitting that bond across a swarm of fake personas cannot multiply voting power, because weight follows the collateral, not the account. To seize governance an attacker must lock more value than all honest agents together, and provable fraud slashes the bond, so the attack costs real capital. That registry is a haven of verifiable identity: scattering trivial tokens, like yarrow seeds on the wind, buys no extra voice.
